title: Suite Control Unit (SCU) - Description and Operation
text:
Suite Control Unit (SCU) - Description and Operation - 1. General

# 1. General

The Suite Control Unit (SCU, P/N DA-SCU-4410) is the seat-level controller for
one first class suite. It drives the backrest actuator (DA-ACT-2201), the legrest
actuator (DA-ACT-2205), the privacy divider drive module (DA-DIV-1180) and the
seat power supply unit (DA-PSU-5150).

The SCU communicates with the Cabin Services System over CAN segment A. Each
suite forms one node. Loss of a single node does not affect the other suites.

title: Suite Control Unit (SCU) - Description and Operation
text:
Suite Control Unit (SCU) - Description and Operation - 2. Operating limits

# 2. Operating limits

| Parameter | Nominal | Caution | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backrest actuator current | 2.2 - 2.8 A | > 3.5 A sustained 10 s | 4.5 A (thermal cutout) |
| Legrest actuator current | 1.6 - 2.2 A | > 3.0 A sustained 10 s | 3.8 A |
| Position error, any axis | < 2 % | > 5 % | 8 % (fault latched) |
| SCU internal temperature | 25 - 45 C | > 60 C | 72 C (derating) |
| CAN segment A error counter | 0 - 5 per hour | > 20 per hour | 100 per hour (bus off) |

title: Suite Control Unit (SCU) - Description and Operation
text:
Suite Control Unit (SCU) - Description and Operation - 3. Built-in test (BITE)

# 3. Built-in test (BITE)

The SCU records a fault code, a timestamp, the flight phase and a sensor snapshot
for every latched fault. BITE memory holds the last 64 events and is downloaded
via the cabin maintenance terminal or streamed to the ground through the aircraft
health link.

A latched fault is cleared only by a successful functional test (see TSM-25-21-40)
or by a power cycle of the suite. A cleared fault that returns within 10 flight
hours must be treated as a repeat defect and must not be closed as no-fault-found.

title: Fault Isolation - Backrest actuator overcurrent (F-25-2101)
section: Fault code F-25-2101 - Recline actuator overcurrent / thermal cutout
text:
Fault Isolation - Backrest actuator overcurrent (F-25-2101) - Fault code F-25-2101 - Recline actuator overcurrent / thermal cutout

# Fault code F-25-2101 - Recline actuator overcurrent / thermal cutout

## Symptom
Backrest moves slowly or stops before the commanded position. SCU logs current
above 3.5 A and position error above 5 %. Cabin crew typically report "seat does
not go flat".

title: Fault Isolation - Backrest actuator overcurrent (F-25-2101)
section: Probable causes, in order of likelihood
text:
Fault Isolation - Backrest actuator overcurrent (F-25-2101) - Probable causes, in order of likelihood

## Probable causes, in order of likelihood
1. Mechanical obstruction in the backrest kinematics (foreign object, seat belt,
   pax personal item) - approx. 45 % of confirmed cases.
2. Gearbox wear in actuator DA-ACT-2201 - approx. 35 %.
3. Degraded connector at the SCU actuator port - approx. 15 %.
4. SCU driver stage failure - approx. 5 %.

title: Fault Isolation - Backrest actuator overcurrent (F-25-2101)
text:
Fault Isolation - Backrest actuator overcurrent (F-25-2101) - Fault isolation procedure

## Fault isolation procedure
1. Visually inspect the kinematics envelope. Remove any obstruction. Repeat a
   full range-of-motion test.
2. Record the actuator current trend over 5 full cycles. A rising trend across
   cycles with no obstruction indicates gearbox wear.
3. Disconnect and inspect the actuator connector for corrosion and bent pins.
   Re-seat and lock. Repeat the test.
4. If the current stays above 3.5 A, replace the actuator DA-ACT-2201.
   Do not replace the SCU first: the historical no-fault-found rate for SCU
   removals on this symptom is high.

title: Fault Isolation - Backrest actuator overcurrent (F-25-2101)
text:
Fault Isolation - Backrest actuator overcurrent (F-25-2101) - Notes on trend data

## Notes on trend data
An actuator whose mean current per cycle has increased by more than 0.8 A over
the last 200 actuation cycles is a wear candidate even when the current is still
inside limits. Plan the replacement at the next base maintenance opportunity
rather than as an unscheduled removal.

title: Fault Isolation - Intermittent CAN segment fault (F-25-2140)
section: Fault code F-25-2140 - CAN segment A error burst / node lost
text:
Fault Isolation - Intermittent CAN segment fault (F-25-2140) - Fault code F-25-2140 - CAN segment A error burst / node lost

# Fault code F-25-2140 - CAN segment A error burst / node lost

## Symptom
Seat control panel unresponsive for seconds to minutes, then normal operation.
SCU logs error bursts on CAN segment A. The defect is very often NOT reproducible
during a static functional test on the ground.

title: Fault Isolation - Intermittent CAN segment fault (F-25-2140)
section: Why this is a no-fault-found trap
text:
Fault Isolation - Intermittent CAN segment fault (F-25-2140) - Why this is a no-fault-found trap

## Why this is a no-fault-found trap
Error bursts on this segment correlate with airframe vibration. In service data,
more than 70 % of bursts occur in taxi, climb or descent, and fewer than 5 %
occur in stable cruise. A ground test without vibration input will therefore
usually pass, and a removed SCU will usually test serviceable in the shop.

Before removing any LRU on this fault code, complete the vibration-correlated
checks below.

title: Fault Isolation - Intermittent CAN segment fault (F-25-2140)
text:
Fault Isolation - Intermittent CAN segment fault (F-25-2140) - Fault isolation procedure

## Fault isolation procedure
1. Download the BITE log and correlate error bursts with flight phase. If the
   bursts cluster in taxi / climb / descent, treat the fault as a wiring or
   connector defect, not as an SCU defect.
2. Inspect connector DA-CON-3390 at both ends of harness segment DA-HRN-7712.
   Look for backed-out pins, corrosion and missing locking clips.
3. Perform a wiggle test on the harness segment while monitoring the CAN error
   counter. An error rate increase during the wiggle test confirms the defect.
4. Measure the bus termination resistance. Nominal is 60 ohm across the segment.
5. Replace the connector kit DA-CON-3390 first. Replace the harness segment
   DA-HRN-7712 only if the wiggle test still produces errors.
6. Remove the SCU only after steps 2 to 5 have been completed and documented.

title: Fault Isolation - Intermittent CAN segment fault (F-25-2140)
text:
Fault Isolation - Intermittent CAN segment fault (F-25-2140) - Fault isolation procedure

## Deferral
If the suite cannot be repaired before departure, see MEL-25-21-02.

title: Fault Isolation - Seat electronics box thermal shutdown (F-23-3401)
section: Fault code F-23-3401 - SEB thermal shutdown
text:
Fault Isolation - Seat electronics box thermal shutdown (F-23-3401) - Fault code F-23-3401 - SEB thermal shutdown

# Fault code F-23-3401 - SEB thermal shutdown

## Symptom
In-flight entertainment at one suite switches off after several hours of cruise
and recovers after a cool-down period. SEB temperature exceeds 78 C before the
shutdown.

## Probable causes
1. Blocked cooling path of the seat electronics box DA-IFE-9002 (dust, pax items
   stored under the seat) - most common.
2. Failed cooling fan inside the SEB.
3. Elevated cabin floor temperature in that zone.

title: Fault Isolation - Seat electronics box thermal shutdown (F-23-3401)
text:
Fault Isolation - Seat electronics box thermal shutdown (F-23-3401) - Procedure

## Procedure
1. Inspect and clean the air inlet and outlet of the SEB. Confirm the required
   free space under the seat pan.
2. Run the SEB self-test with the cabin ground cooling active and record the
   temperature trend for 30 minutes.
3. If the temperature rises above 70 C at idle load, replace the SEB.
4. IFE unavailability at a single suite does not make the suite unsellable, but
   it is a passenger-experience item and must be entered in the cabin log.

title: Fault Isolation - Seat electronics box thermal shutdown (F-23-3401)
text:
Fault Isolation - Seat electronics box thermal shutdown (F-23-3401) - No-fault-found note

## No-fault-found note
A bench test of a removed SEB at ambient temperature will usually pass. Always
attach the in-flight temperature trend to the removal tag.

title: Fault Isolation - Privacy divider does not stow (F-25-2188)
section: Fault code F-25-2188 - Divider drive stall / stow position not reached
text:
Fault Isolation - Privacy divider does not stow (F-25-2188) - Fault code F-25-2188 - Divider drive stall / stow position not reached

# Fault code F-25-2188 - Divider drive stall / stow position not reached

## Safety relevance
The privacy divider must be fully stowed for taxi, take-off and landing. A suite
whose divider does not reach the stowed position is NOT sellable and the seat
must be blocked until repair or an approved deferral is in place.

title: Fault Isolation - Privacy divider does not stow (F-25-2188)
text:
Fault Isolation - Privacy divider does not stow (F-25-2188) - Procedure

## Procedure
1. Check the divider guide rail for debris and for cushion material trapped in
   the rail.
2. Command a full stow cycle and record the drive current and end position.
   Position error above 10 % confirms the defect.
3. Inspect the drive belt of module DA-DIV-1180 for slip marks.
4. Replace DA-DIV-1180 if the belt is worn or the drive stalls under nominal load.
5. After replacement, perform the cabin-safety functional check and have it
   witnessed by a B1 certifying staff member.

title: Service Bulletin - improved locking clip for connector DA-CON-3390
text:
Service Bulletin - improved locking clip for connector DA-CON-3390 - Reason

# Reason

Operators reported intermittent CAN segment A faults (F-25-2140) on suites with
harness segment DA-HRN-7712 installed before serial batch 4400. The root cause
was identified as insufficient retention of the connector locking clip under
vibration.

title: Service Bulletin - improved locking clip for connector DA-CON-3390
text:
Service Bulletin - improved locking clip for connector DA-CON-3390 - Effectivity

# Effectivity

All suites with SCU firmware 3.4.x and harness batches below 4400. Firmware 3.5.0
adds error-burst counters per flight phase, which makes the defect detectable
from the health data before the cabin crew reports it.

# Action

Install the improved locking clip kit at the next base maintenance visit.
Expected effect: reduction of F-25-2140 no-fault-found removals by approximately
half, based on the manufacturer fleet sample. This figure is a synthetic
assumption for the exercise.

title: Task card - inspect and re-seat suite CAN connector
section: Task card: CAN connector inspection and re-seat
text:
Task card - inspect and re-seat suite CAN connector - Task card: CAN connector inspection and re-seat

# Task card: CAN connector inspection and re-seat

Tools: torque screwdriver 0.4-2.0 Nm, contact cleaner, borescope, CAN test set.
Parts (as required): DA-CON-3390 connector kit.

## Steps
1. Safety: confirm cabin power to the suite is isolated. Attach the warning tag.
2. Remove the seat pan access panel. Four captive screws, 1.2 Nm on refit.
3. Locate connector DA-CON-3390 at the SCU port and at the harness junction.
4. Inspect both connectors with the borescope. Record any corrosion, bent or
   backed-out pins with a photograph.
5. Clean the contacts. Re-seat both connectors until the locking clip audibly
   engages.
6. Connect the CAN test set. Run the wiggle test for 3 minutes while monitoring
   the error counter. Acceptance: zero new errors during the wiggle test.
7. Measure the bus termination. Acceptance: 60 ohm plus/minus 6 ohm.

title: Task card - inspect and re-seat suite CAN connector
section: Task card: CAN connector inspection and re-seat
text:
Task card - inspect and re-seat suite CAN connector - Task card: CAN connector inspection and re-seat

8. Refit the access panel. Torque 1.2 Nm.
9. Run the suite functional test: full recline cycle, divider stow cycle, IFE boot.
10. Clear the BITE fault. Record the work order, the measured values and the
    photographs.

## Sign-off
Certifying staff B1 signature required. Attach the CAN test set log to the work order.

title: Task card - replace backrest actuator DA-ACT-2201
text:
Task card - replace backrest actuator DA-ACT-2201 - Task card: backrest actuator replacement

# Task card: backrest actuator replacement

Parts: DA-ACT-2201 (1 ea). Consumables: lock wire, grease MIL-spec equivalent.
Tools: torque wrench 2-25 Nm, actuator alignment jig.

## Steps
1. Isolate suite power. Attach the warning tag.
2. Recline the backrest manually to the service position using the mechanical
   release. Do not force the kinematics.
3. Remove the backrest shroud. Six screws, note the two longer screws at the top.
4. Disconnect the actuator connector. Cap the harness end.
5. Remove the two actuator mounting bolts. Support the actuator while removing
   the second bolt.
6. Fit the new actuator with the alignment jig. Torque the bolts to 18 Nm and
   lock-wire them.
7. Reconnect the actuator. Refit the shroud.
8. Restore power. Run 5 full recline cycles and record the current per cycle.
   Acceptance: mean current below 2.8 A, position error below 2 %.

title: Task card - replace backrest actuator DA-ACT-2201
text:
Task card - replace backrest actuator DA-ACT-2201 - Task card: backrest actuator replacement

9. Update the component record with the removed and installed serial numbers.

## Sign-off
Certifying staff B1 signature required.

title: No-Fault-Found policy for cabin LRU removals (synthetic)
text:
No-Fault-Found policy for cabin LRU removals (synthetic) - Purpose

# Purpose

Reduce unnecessary removals of cabin LRUs and the associated shop cost, without
dispatching an aircraft with an unresolved cabin-safety defect.

# Decision rules used in this exercise

1. A removal is justified when at least one of the following holds:
   a) the fault is reproducible in a functional test on the ground, or
   b) the trend data shows a monotonic degradation over at least three flight
      legs, or
   c) the fault is cabin-safety relevant (divider stow, seat lock) and cannot be
      cleared by the applicable task card.
2. If none of these hold, the defect is classified as NOT REPRODUCIBLE. The
   required action is the connector / harness task card plus continued monitoring
   for the next 10 flight legs, not an LRU removal.
3. Every removal request for a rotable LRU must carry an NFF risk score between

title: No-Fault-Found policy for cabin LRU removals (synthetic)
text:
No-Fault-Found policy for cabin LRU removals (synthetic) - Purpose

0 and 1 with a written justification and the evidence used.
4. An NFF risk above 0.6 requires a second opinion from the component owner
   (manufacturer or MRO) before the removal is released. This is the external
   request path across the organisational boundary.
5. Cost anchors for the trade-off: a blocked first class suite costs the airline
   approximately EUR 10,000 per leg in lost revenue, an unscheduled removal
   approximately EUR 3,800, and a shop test that finds nothing approximately
   EUR 1,450. These are synthetic planning figures for the exercise.

title: Ground time and slot rules for cabin work (synthetic)
text:
Ground time and slot rules for cabin work (synthetic) - Rules

# Rules

1. Cabin work may only be planned in a ground slot that is at least the task
   duration plus 30 minutes of buffer.
2. Work that needs cabin power isolation may not run in parallel with catering
   or cleaning in the same zone.
3. Stations with line maintenance can perform connector and software tasks.
   Rotable LRU replacement requires either base maintenance or an MRO partner
   with the corresponding capability.
4. If the required part is not on stock at the arrival station, the planner must
   compare: expedited freight (surcharge approx. EUR 2,200) against blocking the
   suite for the next legs (approx. EUR 10,000 per leg).
5. A task that would delay departure by more than 20 minutes must be escalated
   to the network control centre. Delay cost is assumed at approx. EUR 95 per
   minute for this exercise.
